question.prompt:
Semicircle \(\overset{\frown}{AB}\) has center \(C\) and radius \(1.\) Point \(D\) is on \(\overset{\frown}{AB}\) and \(CD\perp AB.\) Extend \(\overline{BD}\) and \(\overline{AD}\) to \(E\) and \(F,\) respectively, so that circular arcs \(\overset{\frown}{AE}\) and \(\overset{\frown}{BF}\) have \(B\) and \(A\) as their respective centers. Circular arc \(\overset{\frown}{EF}\) has center \(D.\) The area of the shaded “smile,” \(AEFBDA,\) is

[Figure 1](figures/1992_AMC_12_Q26_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
First find the area enclosed by the straight diameter \(AB\) and the outer arcs \(AE,EF,FB\). Subtracting the original semicircle will then leave the shaded smile.

Since \(C\) is the center and \(CD\perp AB\), triangles \(ACD\) and \(BCD\) are right triangles with both legs equal to \(1\). Thus their acute angles are \(45^\circ\), and the Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
AD=BD=\sqrt2,\qquad AB=2.
\]
The arc \(AE\) has center \(B\), so \(BE=BA=2\). Because \(E\) lies beyond \(D\) on \(BD\),
\[
DE=BE-BD=2-\sqrt2.
\]
Similarly, \(DF=2-\sqrt2\). Also, \(\angle ADB=90^\circ\); extending both sides through \(D\) gives \(\angle EDF=90^\circ\).

Consider the two \(45^\circ\) sectors bounded by \(BA,BE\) and by \(AB,AF\). Each has radius \(2\), so each has area
\[
\frac{45}{360}\pi(2)^2=\frac{\pi}{2}.
\]
Their overlap is exactly triangle \(ABD\): their angular wedges intersect in that triangle, which lies inside both radius-\(2\) sectors. Its base is \(AB=2\) and its height is \(CD=1\), so its area is \(1\). The union of these sectors consequently has area \(\pi-1\).

Adding the quarter-circle sector \(EDF\) fills the remaining part of the outer region. It meets the two previous sectors only along its straight sides, so no area is counted twice. Finally subtract the semicircle of radius \(1\). The shaded area is
\[
\begin{aligned}
S&=\pi-1+\frac{\pi}{4}(2-\sqrt2)^2-\frac{\pi}{2}\\
&=\pi-1+\frac{\pi}{4}(6-4\sqrt2)-\frac{\pi}{2}\\
&=\boxed{2\pi-\pi\sqrt2-1}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Combine sectors and subtract the semicircle
